title: Faster recovery of Atlantic main-development-region storm cold wakes after 2000 appears only in ERA5 peak-normalised metrics, not in OISST or drifters; 2021-2025 wakes lasted longer (1982-2025)
abstract: Question: does the reported faster recovery of tropical-cyclone cold wakes in the Atlantic main development region (MDR, 10-20 N, 80-20 W, June-October) after 2000 (John et al. 2025, ERA5 SST) survive an independent product, drifters, the 2007-09-01 ERA5 input switch (HadISST2 to OSTIA) and 2021-2025? Approach: we built cold-wake series at 2,959 IBTrACS MDR fixes (236 storms, 1982-2025) in ERA5 and NOAA OISST v2.1 on identical fixes, compared both with 113,363 NOAA Global Drifter Program values in North Atlantic wakes, and used storm bootstrap intervals. Results: ERA5 gave the reported direction: per-fix normalised recovery at days 18-22 rose by +0.37 (95% interval +0.01 to +0.74) and the rise from peak to days 20-40 by +0.155 C (+0.050 to +0.251) from 1982-2000 to 2001-2020; the composite-normalised day-20 change was +0.19 (-0.18 to +0.53). OISST on the same fixes showed +0.11 (-0.16 to +0.37) and -0.05 C (-0.18 to +0.08). ERA5 minus OISST in the rise metric was -0.37 and -0.38 C in 1982-2000 and 2001-2006 (HadISST2 era) but -0.07 C in 2008-2020: before the switch ERA5 had a 0.14 C weaker wake peak. At days 18-22 the products agreed within 0.05 C in all epochs. Drifters showed that ERA5 under-cooled the wake at days 3-15 more before 2007 (0.13 and 0.07 C) than after (0.05 and 0.04 C), that both products match drifters within 0.05 C at days 15-40, and that the drifter fraction of the wake left at days 15-25 did not change (+0.02, -0.34 to +0.41). In 2021-2025 the wake at days 20-40 was 0.27 C (ERA5) and 0.23 C (OISST) colder than in 2008-2020, so recovery did not continue to become faster. Limitations: the pre-registered within-ERA5 step test failed (the ERA5 change appears already in 2001-2006 and a step fits no better than a trend), so the input switch alone does not explain it; drifters are sparse in the MDR and before 1992; our wake definition differs from the unpublished original code; OSTIA reprocessed was not tested. Conclusion: we find no robust evidence for a trend in MDR cold-wake recovery in 1982-2025; the reported change depends on ERA5 and on normalisation by a peak that ERA5 measured differently before 2007.
